title: WPMS/440/2016 of Karam Vir AND OTHERS Vs Devi Prasad AND OTHERS

paras.text:
Reserved Order
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Recall Application No.815 of 2016
In
Writ Petition (M/S) No.440 of 2016
Karam Vir & others
 ÖÖ. Petitioner
Versus
Devi Prasad & others
 ÖÖ Respondents
Mr. Sudhir Kumar, Adv. for the petitioner.
Mr. P.C. Bisht, S.C., for the State.
Mr. M.S. Tyagi, Advocate for the respondent nos.4 and 6/applicants.
Dated: 17.11.2017
Honíble Rajiv Sharma , J.
Recall Application No.815 of 2016
 The present recall application has been filed to
recall the judgment dated 6.10.2016 passed in WPMS
No.440 of 2016.
 Case of the applicants/respondent nos.4 to 6
is that no notices were ever issued to them and the
judgment dated 6.10.2016 is ex parte qua them. It would
be necessary to discuss the facts in detail to effectively
adjudicate the application.
 Father of the petitioner nos.1 and 2, namely,
Gyan Chand raised the loan from respondent no.7-
Cooperative Society. Respondent nos.1 to 3 are the sons
of late Badri Dutt. Respondent no.4-Smt. Manorama
Devi is the widow of Bhagwati Prasad and respondent
nos.5 and 6, namely, Pankaj and Sushil are the
grandsons of Badri Dutt. The sale certificate was issued
in favour of Badri Dutt on 30.6.1977. Gyand Chand
moved an application under Sections Order XXI Rule 99,

2
100, 101 and 105 of the Code of Civil Procedure for
setting aside the auction. Application was dismissed by
the Assistant Collector as well as by the Commissioner.
The Board of Revenue allowed the revision vide order
dated 19.10.1982. The operative portion of the order
reads as under: -
ìIt has been held by our High Court in Writ Petition
No.1002 of 1978-Muneshwar Baksh Singh vs.
Farzand and others that the provisions of Rule 285
are mandatory and if the balance amount is not
deposited within 15 days, the amount deposited
earlier shall be forfeited to the Government and the
property shall be resold. Since in this case, we do
not find even any factor which could prevent the
auction purchaser from fulfilling his obligation, the
sale proceedings have to be declared void. In the
result, the sale proceedings are set aside and the
case is remanded to the Collector for further recovery
proceedings in accordance with law.î
 Mr. Badri Dutt challenged the decision dated
19.10.1982 by filing WPMS No.698 of 1983 before the
Hon. Allahabad High Court. It was transferred to this
Court and assigned a new number i.e. WPMS No.261 of
2001. It was dismissed by this Court on 13.12.2010.
The SLP was also dismissed on 22.7.2013.
 Mr. Badri Dutt filed Suit No.51/1977 which
was partly decreed on 13.7.1978. Appeal preferred
against the decree dated 13.7.1978 was allowed on
15.7.1980. Second Appeal No.1818 of 1980 was
preferred before the Allahabad High Court which was
transferred to this Court and it was re-numbered as S.A.
No.353 of 2001. The second appeal was dismissed by
this Court vide judgment dated 28.11.2005.

3
 Mr. Gyan Chand also filed Civil Suit No.41 of
2010. It was decreed on 1.2.2012 and the private
respondents were restrained from interfering with the
possession of the plaintiff. Application was filed by Gyan
Chand for correction of revenue record. It was dismissed
by the Assistant Collector on 19.6.2015. Revision was
also dismissed on 20.1.2016. It is in these circumstances
the writ petition was heard and the judgment was
pronounced on 06.10.2016.
 Respondent nos.1 and 2 Devi Prasad and
Virendra Prasad are the sons of Badri Dutt who were
duly represented by their advocate. The state of Badri
Dutt was duly and adequately represented by respondent
nos.1 and 2. The respondents have not filed any counter
affidavit to the writ petition. Respondent nos.4 to 6 are
the legal heirs of Badri Dutt. The interest of respondent
nos.1 to 3 and nos.4 to 6 was common since Badri Dutt
has purchased the land by way of auction in the year
1975 which was set aside by the Board of Revenue on
19.10.1982. It cannot be believed that the respondent
nos.4 to 6 were not aware of the proceedings pending
before this Court.
 Accordingly, there is no merit in the recall
application and the same is hereby dismissed.
 (Rajiv Sharma, J.)
Rdang
